rows.row: parts, and how they depend on each other
rows.file_10_quote: \(V\) is a set of ports, each with a nonempty value domain \(X_v\). A valuation is an element of \(X_D=\prod_v X_v\). \(J\) indexes components; each component \(j\) has a footprint \(V_j\subseteq V\).
rows.note: Also Part 0: "An explanation is a **question-relevant organization of dependencies**". Two looser edges: an organization is the six-tuple (V,(X_v),J,B,A,L), so it carries the boundary conditions and the admitted edits as well, which the skill maps separately at rows 2, 3 and 5; and "ports" glossed as "the ties between them" is loose, since ports are value slots and components tie to each other by sharing them.

rows.row: a change to the world; a poke
rows.file_10_quote: A deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports. An edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning that port; it does not add an equation beside an incompatible one. A changed rule is a changed component.
rows.note: The gloss's three examples (set a value, remove a piece, swap a rule) are file 10's three. "A change to the world" is narrower than the theory's edit: Part 0 says "An admitted change need not be a physical intervention. Removing an axiom, dropping a constraint, or changing a dimension are edits on an organization". by-domain.md covers that for proofs; this row does not.

rows.file_10_quote: The **contract** \(C\subseteq A\times B\) is the set of admitted edit–boundary pairs the claim ranges over; it contains the baseline \((1,b_0)\).
rows.note: Exact for the gloss's first half; the second half ("left off openly") is the non-vacuity clause quoted at row 12. A contract is edit-boundary *pairs* and contains the baseline; the skill's "change list" carries the edits, with the baseline going to row 5's "starting state".

rows.file_10_quote: A production question has a \(\mathcal Q\) that reads an output port and a \(C\) containing interventions on upstream ports. An identification question has a \(\mathcal Q\) that computes a fibre and a \(C\) containing edits to the observed value. An obstruction question has a \(\mathcal Q\) that returns a reachability truth value.
rows.note: The gloss's three examples are these three, in order.

rows.theory_term: question (target, contract, baseline, query, obligations, provenance)
rows.file_10_quote:
A question is

\[
p=(D,\ C,\ b_0,\ \mathcal Q,\ O_p,\ \rho_p).
\]
rows.note: The six components named in the term column are file 10's six. But the gloss covers four (D, C, b_0, Q). Obligations are named here and glossed nowhere, and no other row says what they do, though the theory's "\(O_p\) is the set of obligations being addressed or protected" and Part XI's "protected obligations \(P\), fixed for the comparison" are the carrier for the skill's mark *fixed*. See left_out.

rows.file_10_quote: The respect of a question, from its query (Part III).
rows.note: Term verbatim (Part XIV's dependence list; the Part III heading is "The respect is the query"). The gloss's five respects and its "not by a label" clause are exact: "What a question asks — production, identification, obstruction, rule-status, purpose-achievement — is fixed by the type of \(\mathcal Q\) and the shape of \(C\), not by a label." SKILL.md Step 1 lists six kinds; the sixth ("Why is there none of it?") is not a respect but the Part VII question shape, which row 36 maps. Two rows for two different places in the theory.

rows.file_10_quote: where \(\pi:X_D\to X_E\) on the stated scope, \(\tau\) translates edits, \(\sigma\) translates boundaries, and \(\lambda\) assigns each component of \(E\) a subnetwork of \(D\) with a port translation.
rows.note: The gloss's "pairing between parts" is λ; "how changes to one translate to the other" is τ. Held.

rows.row: each part moves as its counterpart moves
rows.file_10_quote: **Component fidelity.** For every active component \(k\) of \(E\) with anchor subnetwork \(\lambda(k)\subseteq D\), and every \((a,b)\in C\), the relation obtained by imposing the constraints of \(\lambda(k)\) and projecting away its hidden ports equals the component relation of \(k\) under the translated edit
rows.note: Name and label both verbatim; the gloss is the condition in plain words. Held.

rows.row: the whole moves as the whole moves
rows.file_10_quote: A transport is **faithful on \(C\)** when it satisfies the component and global fidelity conditions of Part V.
rows.note: I expected "global fidelity" to be the skill's coinage, because in Part V (F2) sits unnamed under the bold heading "Component fidelity"; the name is file 10's own, one Part earlier. The gloss's "no shared tie has been lost" is file 10's "(F2) prevents a set of locally correct pieces from hiding a lost shared constraint." One clause of (F2) is not glossed: "\(\tau(1)=1,\quad \tau(a_2a_1)=\tau(a_2)\tau(a_1)\)", that composed changes must translate to composed changes. Part VIII's functional-transport theorem is what makes checking one change at a time enough; neither the clause nor the theorem has a row.

rows.row: it answers the question that was asked
rows.file_10_quote: The query \(\mathcal Q\) is held fixed; an account of a different query is not an account of this one.
rows.note: Name, label and gloss all exact. Held.

rows.row: the answer is not hidden in the starting points
rows.file_10_quote: There exists \((a,b)\in C\) that removes or replaces a nonempty block of \(\Gamma\) while preserving the other boundary conditions, under which the answer profile changes or ceases to be determined in the claimed way.
rows.note: Held. File 10 requires a change removing or replacing a nonempty *block*; the gloss says "a working part", which is the singleton case (the block case is rows 16 and 19). File 10's "moving an assertion from an input slot into a component named \"law\" does not discharge this" is the skill's "nature", "law", "tendency" list.

rows.row: the change list is not empty and says what it leaves out
rows.file_10_quote: **Non-vacuity.** \(\operatorname{Sol}_D(1,b_0)\neq\varnothing\). The contract \(C\) is a declared subset of the physically admitted edits, and every physically admitted edit excluded from \(C\) is excluded by a stated scope, not silently.
rows.note: The gloss is exact for non-vacuity: baseline possible, exclusions stated. The plain word's first half is not. File 10 routes the empty-in-effect contract through the other condition: "A contract consisting only of relabelings, or excluding every change under which the active commitments could matter to \(\mathcal Q\), does not satisfy non-circular dependence and is therefore not a contract on which an account can be claimed." A reader tracing "the change list is not empty" back lands on non-vacuity and will not find it there; it is at row 11.
Five conjuncts, as the gloss says. Held.

rows.file_10_quote: An explanatory candidate for question \(p\) is an organization \(E\), a transport \(t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda)\) from \(D\) to \(E\), and an identified set \(\Gamma\) of active commitments in \(E\).
rows.note: Held. "Identified" carries the skill's point that the owner says which parts are claimed to do the work.

rows.row: a set of parts that is enough
rows.note: The definition and label are exact and the gloss restates them. The phrase "support set" is not in file 10, which writes "a support", "minimal support", "**Infinitary support.**"; a harmless coinage.

rows.row: a group you cannot remove together
rows.file_10_quote: A block may be critical while no singleton in it is.
rows.note: Exact, with the definition (B) above it. This is also the theory's carrier for file 32's new "held, jointly with" wording (change 3, answering H64 kind 3); the word list does not connect the mark to it, because it maps critical blocks to a removal test rather than to a mark.

rows.file_10_quote: **Redundant routes.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\},\{b\},\{a,b\}\}\): each is contributory, neither indispensable.
rows.note: The gloss is the second half in plain words. The one mark of the eight that has a term of its own. Held.

rows.row: an added part that breaks it
rows.file_10_quote: **Interference.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\}\}\): the full candidate fails although a subset succeeds.
rows.note: Exact. File 10's next sentence, "\(b\) is not made \"not a commitment\" to repair this", is the skill's refusal to drop an inconvenient part, and has no row.

rows.file_10_quote: **Infinitary support.** \(\Gamma=\{d_n:|x|\le 1/n\}\): every unbounded index set determines \(x=0\); no minimal support and no singleton witness exists.
rows.note: Exact, including "no minimal support" for the gloss's "no smallest sufficient set". Held.

rows.row: where a variation tips it from passing to failing
rows.note: Exact, including that it is a set of pairs, which the gloss keeps. The skill names no test for it; it surfaces only inside *Pull* ("what would show that the line was drawn in the wrong place") and *Check the patches* ("swap the new limit for a neighbour").

rows.file_10_quote: **Hard-to-vary.** For explanatory jobs \(F\subseteq F'\), \(\operatorname{Pres}(F')\subseteq\operatorname{Pres}(F)\), where \(\operatorname{Pres}(F)=\{v\in\mathcal V:\forall f\in F,\operatorname{Account}(E_v,f)\}\).
rows.note: The term is verbatim and occurs once in file 10. In the definition each \(f\) sits where a question \(p\) sits in Account(·,·), so a job is a question the candidate must be an account for; the gloss's "things the explanation has to account for" is a fair plain rendering of that. What the row leaves unmapped is Step 2's requirement that a job be "put as a contrast: why this *and not that*". Its nearest footing in file 10 is Part V's "An account whose only substantive contrast is one that no physically admitted edit realizes fails non-vacuity", which has no row. See left_out.

rows.file_10_quote: \(\operatorname{Pres}(F)=\{v\in\mathcal V:\forall f\in F,\operatorname{Account}(E_v,f)\}\)
rows.note: \(\mathcal V\) is "a declared family \(\mathcal V\) of organization edits", so "versions of the explanation" is right, and "still do every job" is the universal quantifier. Held.

rows.theory_term: Hard-to-vary: for F ⊆ F′, Pres(F′) ⊆ Pres(F)
rows.file_10_quote: More reach constrains variation; the containment need not be strict; counting jobs is not a warrant.
rows.note: The tightest row in the list. All three clauses of the gloss are file 10's own sentence, including the word "reach" and the ban on counting that the skill's stance and traps repeat. Held.

rows.file_10_quote: at any level of detail, a *kind* is nothing over and above how a component responds to the changes that level admits. Two components no admitted change can separate are one kind at that level, whatever labels anyone attaches to them.
rows.note: Heading "Kinds are edit-signatures" verbatim, and Derivation 1's corollary is stronger than the gloss: "The word \"kind\" is therefore eliminable from the definition of an account, and its elimination loses no case." Note the theory's claim is about kind-*labels* adding no discriminating power, which is what the skill's trap says ("If no change to the world could tell the label from a different one"). Held.

rows.row: the same explanation at this level
rows.file_10_quote: **Claim.** Two candidates \(\mathcal E,\mathcal E'\) for the same \(p\) that both satisfy (F1), (F2), and (A) on \(C\) are one account at grain \(C\): their components are pairwise of one kind on \(C\) and their answer profiles coincide.
rows.note: Derivation 2's premise is that both candidates *are* accounts on C; the gloss states the other direction, that indistinguishability makes them one. The skill's actual use ("If no change on the list can [tell them apart], they are the same explanation at this level") is carried by (K) — "Two components \(j,j'\) are **of one kind on \(C\)** when there is a bijection of their footprints under which \(\operatorname{sig}_C(j)\) and \(\operatorname{sig}_C(j')\) coincide" — and by Derivation 2's consequence, "A claim that two such candidates \"really\" differ is a claim that some admitted change separates them, and must supply it." The verdict survives; the row cites the premise-heavier half. Also: "grain \(C\)" — here the grain is the contract, which no row states.

rows.file_10_quote: produced by blind variation and survival on a history of predictions
rows.note: "Blind" is file 10's word. The apparatus is Part IV: "a population \(\mathcal T\) of candidate transports, a variation operator \(\mu\) on \(\mathcal T\), a finite history \(H\subseteq C\) of edit–boundary pairs actually encountered, and a survival condition requiring fidelity on \(H\)". Held.

rows.file_10_quote: **Constructed.** There is an episode (Part X) whose construction witness prepares \(t\), and in which \(t\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target.
rows.note: "With the target in view" is "available as a represented target"; "and criticism" is Part 0's "produced by an episode of conjecture and criticism". Held.

rows.file_10_quote: **Declared.** Neither of the above. The transport is entered into the model by its author.
rows.note: Held. File 10 adds a restriction the row does not carry: "Declaration is permitted only as a modelling convenience, and a claim about creativity cannot rest on it." That is the theory's reason why *asserted* holds nothing, which the skill states flatly instead ("someone simply said so").

rows.row: held only where it was tested
rows.file_10_quote: A correspondence produced by selection is faithful where it was tested and unconstrained where it was not.
rows.note: Exact, and in file 10 it is proved rather than assumed: "For every \((a,b)\in C\setminus H\) there exists a transport \(t'\), also surviving on \(H\), with a different value at \((a,b)\)." Held.

rows.file_10_quote:
a **violation** occurs when fidelity fails at \((a,b)\);
- **surprise** is a violation at \((a,b)\notin H\).
rows.note: Both terms verbatim, and the gloss is the definition. Held.

rows.row: re-tune, or build a new part
rows.file_10_quote: The two responses — extend \(H\) and re-tune, or construct a new transport — are the difference between learning and creating
rows.note: "Learning versus creating" is file 10's own phrase (Derivation 4's consequence); both response names are bold terms in Part IV; Derivation 10 works the case. Held.

rows.file_10_quote: A reversed calculation — identification presented as production — fails (F2) under the production contract: intervening on the upstream port changes the target's downstream value but not the calculation's.
rows.note: Term verbatim. The skill's Reverse test is this plus Part VII's "Direction is derived from the admitted edits; the nouns \"pole\" and \"shadow\" fix nothing", and the pole-and-shadow case in the skill's in-depth file is file 10's own worked construction. Held.

rows.row: what the evidence can hold in place
rows.file_10_quote: The fibre at \(y\) is \(Z_y=g^{-1}(y)\). The feature is identified at \(y\) exactly when \(Z_y\neq\varnothing\land|f[Z_y]|=1\). (I1)
rows.note: The gloss is (I1) in plain words: every state giving those readings agrees on the feature. The skill's two-scales case is file 10's: "the kernel is spanned by \((1,-1,-1)\); the readings identify \(b_B-b_A\) and not \(x\)", and its circularity warning is file 10's "\"Set \(b_B=0\) because it gives the mass I favour\" is not an inference from the readings". Held.

rows.file_10_quote: (I4) Repeating rows changes no kernel; an independent calibration can.
rows.note: Exact; the gloss's "independent check" for "independent calibration". Held.

rows.file_10_quote: For allowed steps \(R\) and an invariant \(I\) with \(zRz'\Rightarrow I(z)=I(z')\), no allowed path joins states of different invariant value. (O1) Equal values do not establish reachability.
rows.note: Both terms exact. The skill carries (O1)'s caution in its in-depth file ("two things matching on that unchanging quantity does *not* show you can get from one to the other") and the coins case is file 10's. Held.

rows.file_10_quote: This is the semantics' treatment of eliminative explanation; it is offered as adequate and is listed under attack (B) as a place where it may not be.
rows.note: Heading verbatim. "Tested by putting the missing piece in" is "An account is faithful when introducing those components changes the answer in \(E\) as it does in \(D\), and their absence leaves both unchanged." The self-marked weakness is passed on, which is what this file's own Traps require. Held.

rows.file_10_quote: **Historical index.** A proposition indexed to a contract remains that proposition when a later theory changes the current contract. A new index is a new claim.
rows.note: "Frozen" is file 10's word: "An assessment is an event with a frozen contract" (Part 0, grievance 10), and Derivation 7 is titled "The frozen assessment and the moving question are consistent". Held.

rows.file_10_quote: What is prohibited is changing \(C\) or \(\mathcal Q\) during an assessment without recording that the claim has changed.
rows.note: The gloss's "the change list or what is asked" is \(C\) or \(\mathcal Q\) exactly; "A new index is a new claim" is Part VIII. Held.

rows.theory_term: changing the index without recording it
rows.file_10_quote: Goalpost-moving is the act of changing the index without recording the change, and it is a failure of the record, not a licensed operation of the semantics.
rows.note: Term and gloss both all but verbatim. Held. One slip of form, not substance: the Where column gives "Derivation 7" alone where every other row gives a Part; Derivation 7 is in Part XVI.

rows.file_10_quote: Finding the right question is a creative act on the same footing as answering one.
rows.note: "A **constructed** contract is the result of an episode with a construction witness" is Part III verbatim, and Derivation 5 proves a contract can be the content that is built. Held. This is the theory's own claim to novelty (Part 0: "question-finding is at least half of creativity"), and the skill uses it only lightly, in Step 1 and in the note that a changed question is a new claim.

rows.row: a failed test knocks down the bundle
rows.file_10_quote: **What a test refutes.** For \(T\land B\land I\Rightarrow O\), an established \(\neg O\) yields \(\neg(T\land B\land I)\) and nothing narrower. (K3)
rows.note: The gloss's "predicting wrongly ... only \"not all three\" follows" is exact, and correctly restricted to a failure. But file 10 never says what T, B and I stand for; "theory and background and test set-up" is the skill's reading of three undefined letters. It is the conventional reading and is very likely what was meant; the row does not mark it as supplied. Compare row 53, which reads the same term more widely.

rows.row: a sign is not yet a criticism
rows.file_10_quote: An adverse signal is not a criticism until an organization represents how it bears.
rows.note: Exact, with the formal condition above it: "\(\operatorname{Bearing}(c,z,p)\iff\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E_c,p_\delta)\)" — a criticism must itself be an account of the defect, which is sharper than the skill's plain words and unused by the skill. Held.

rows.row: removing a reason removes support, not truth
rows.file_10_quote: Withdrawing a premise removes a license; it does not make the conclusion false.
rows.note: Exact (file 10 "license", the row "licence"). Held.

rows.file_10_quote: Negation exchanges them; missing evidence stays missing.
rows.note: The gloss draws the consequence instead of quoting: under negation the for- and against-receipts swap, but a gap stays a gap, so an empty \(N_j(\phi)\) never becomes a receipt in \(P_j(\phi)\). That is exactly the skill's "Absence of a counter-case is not evidence for." Held.

rows.row: near enough, and how error grows
rows.file_10_quote: (T2) Without a modulus, no accumulated bound follows. An exact question is not silently replaced by an approximate one.
rows.note: Held. The "modulus" is the constant of "an \(L\)-Lipschitz next-step map" in \(e_n\le\varepsilon\sum_{k<n}L^k\); the gloss's "bound on growth" is a fair plain word for it.

rows.file_10_quote: **Claim.** If \(M_0,M_1\) have the same input–output projection and differ on an account claim, no function of the projection agrees with the claim on both.
rows.note: Held, and also Part 0: "Two systems with identical outputs and different internal routes are different organizations here, and the semantics says so." Derivation 9 is also the right anchor for row 53's claim about a passed test, which row 53 does not cite.

rows.row: where a job came from: given, fixed, added
rows.theory_term: provenance of a contract (declared, selected, constructed)
rows.file_10_quote: \(\rho_p\in\{\text{declared},\ \text{selected},\ \text{constructed}\}\), with the witness required by Part IV. A **declared** contract is stipulated by the modeller.
rows.note: MISMATCH, the widest in the list, in three parts. (1) File 10 gives provenance to the *contract*: one \(\rho_p\) per question. "Explanatory jobs \(F\)" (Part VI) carry no provenance field, so the gloss's "and so each job in it" is the skill's inference, not the theory's step. (2) The three skill tags are not the three theory values. *Given* and *added* are both **declared** (stipulated, by owner or by tester), and the theory's *selected* and *constructed* have no skill tag, so the skill cannot record of a job the one thing the theory most wants recorded of a question: that it was found rather than stipulated (Derivation 5; row 40). (3) *Fixed* is not a provenance. It answers whether a job is up for test, not where it came from — and file 32 says so in its own new paragraph: "*borrowed* and *fixed* are not provenances." The theory's carrier for it exists and is unmapped: "\(O_p\) is the set of obligations being addressed or protected" (Part III) and "For claimed obligations \(O\) and protected obligations \(P\), fixed for the comparison" (Part XI). See left_out.

rows.theory_term: Pres(F) depends on the job set F
rows.file_10_quote: \(\operatorname{Pres}(F)=\{v\in\mathcal V:\forall f\in F,\operatorname{Account}(E_v,f)\}\)
rows.note: The term column holds a true observation about a definition, not a term of file 10; the first sentence of the gloss follows from that definition and is safe. The second sentence — "A part held only by a doubtful job is held relative to that job" — has no footing in file 10: there is no notion of a doubtful job, and no notion of a part being *held*. The theory's words for that are in the finite monotone theorem ("the critical singletons", "the globally indispensable ones"), which has no row. File 32's widening of *held if* to a part in doubt likewise has no term here, though critical blocks (row 16) carry the joint case.

rows.row: parts that pull against each other
rows.file_10_quote: **Interference.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\}\}\): the full candidate fails although a subset succeeds.
rows.note: The gloss restates interference correctly, but interference is already row 18 under a different plain word, and *Pull* is a different act: "Does making one stronger make another weaker? ... say which one gives way and where, and what would show that the line was drawn in the wrong place." Strength-trading is not set-membership failure, and "where the line is" is Boundary (D), row 20. The fairest reading, which I tested and which holds, is that Pull is a way of *hunting* interference and also asks a boundary question; on that reading the row is half right and cites half its support. Two parts can trade off with every subset still an account, and two parts can interfere with no dimension along which either is "stronger".

rows.theory_term: non-vacuity: every excluded change is excluded by a stated scope
rows.file_10_quote: every physically admitted edit excluded from \(C\) is excluded by a stated scope, not silently
rows.note: The quoted clause is verbatim, and "and here also measured" is honest signposting that the gauge is the skill's own addition; "catch-all" and "gauge" are absent from file 10 (checked). But the anchor looks wrong. A catch-all part does not *exclude* a change, it *absorbs* one: it is a commitment that constrains nothing, and file 10's nearest words are Part II's "A deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports" and non-circularity's demand for a change that makes the answer move. Non-vacuity is a condition on the contract; a catch-all is a part.

rows.row: a fitted part cannot be confirmed on the cases it was fitted to
rows.file_10_quote: A correspondence produced by selection is faithful where it was tested and unconstrained where it was not.
rows.note: Read strictly, the plain word is not Derivation 3's claim: Derivation 3 says a selected transport is undetermined *off* its history, and on the history it is faithful — that much the selection does establish. The gloss's word "new" ("says nothing *new* about that history") is the right hedge and rescues it. The second citation carries by analogy only: (I4) is about a measurement kernel in Part VII, not about a transport, and the row does not say it is reaching across.

rows.file_10_quote: An evidence leaf is a reference to an event with an interpreted claim. A receipt is a derivation tree over leaves.
rows.note: "Each claim traces to an event" is exact. The four tags are the skill's own: file 10 separates leaves from derived nodes, so *worked out* maps to a non-leaf, but it does not divide leaves into seen, claimed and recalled. "A memory is a different event from a reading" is an application of "a reference to an event", not something file 10 says. A useful addition, not a mapped term.

rows.row: the three layers of a home-made test: the thing, the rig, the inputs
rows.file_10_quote: For \(T\land B\land I\Rightarrow O\), an established \(\neg O\) yields \(\neg(T\land B\land I)\) and nothing narrower. (K3)
rows.note: MISMATCH on one word: "passed". (K3) is stated for an established \(\neg O\) only. From \(T\land B\land I\Rightarrow O\) together with \(O\), nothing follows, so (K3) says nothing at all about a test that passes, and the row's "A failed or passed test bears on theory, background and set-up together" reads it wider than it is written. The skill's point is sound — testing-against-cases: "A pass, or a fix, can come from any layer" — but its footing is Derivation 9 and Part V's "A true mechanism guessed for bad reasons satisfies (E)", neither of which the row cites. Row 41 glosses the same term correctly as failure only, so the list disagrees with itself about (K3)'s reach. The three named layers are also the skill's reading of T, B, I, which file 10 leaves undefined.

rows.row: freeze the rig after one case; count the patches
rows.file_10_quote: a finite history \(H\subseteq C\) of edit–boundary pairs actually encountered, and a survival condition requiring fidelity on \(H\)
rows.note: The gloss applies Derivation 3 to a test rig by treating the rig as a transport selected on a one-case history. File 10's selected provenance is a claim about a physical history of transports between organizations — "**Selection in the physical module.** A selected provenance \(\operatorname{Sel}(t;\mathcal T,\mu,H)\) is a claim about a physical history" — and does not extend itself to rigs; the extension is the skill's and is not marked as one. "Count the patches" has no term in file 10.

rows.row: every change after research is a new claim
rows.file_10_quote: A proposition indexed to a contract remains that proposition when a later theory changes the current contract.
rows.note: The same mapping as row 38 under a different plain word; both hold. Part XI states the research case exactly: "A later narrowing of that contract to rescue adequacy is a new claim at a new index, and does not retroactively satisfy (EK)."

rows.row: watch the part as well as the outcome; a measurement moves when only its reading is changed
rows.theory_term: measurement and causal signatures; roles are derived
rows.file_10_quote: a **measurement** has a signature invariant under interventions on the measured port and variable under edits to the measuring relation;
rows.note: The tightest technical row after "hard to vary; reach". The skill's "change only how it is read or reported" is file 10's observation edit word for word: "A port is an **observation** when \(A\) contains an edit that alters the relation reporting it without altering what it reports." And the skill's "The thing that produces the outcome stays put under that change" is file 10's "a **causal assignment** ... is invariant under observation edits". Held. The heading "Roles are derived" also carries the skill's Reverse test: "The direction of an organization is a consequence of which edits it admits, not a stipulation."

rows.row: a held limit carries its reason inside the explanation
rows.theory_term: hard-to-vary over scope: Pres(F) under edits to the contract
rows.file_10_quote: For a declared family \(\mathcal V\) of organization edits,
rows.note: "Hard-to-vary over scope" is not in file 10, and Part VI's \(\mathcal V\) is a family of *organization* edits, not contract edits, so "Pres(F) under edits to the contract" is a construction rather than a term. The theory does permit the construction — Derivation 5 makes a contract an organization with "admitted edits (add or remove a change; alter \(\mathcal Q\))" — but Part VIII then makes each such edit a new index rather than a variation inside one frozen assessment. The skill itself keeps clear of that: it tests only limits sitting inside the explanation ("the yeast slows in the cold") and marks a limit that "only says what is being asked about" free. So the gloss ("A limit is a part; swap it and see what breaks") is sound for the kind the skill actually tests, and the term column points at the other kind.

rows.row: not truth, not a score, not elegance
rows.theory_term: "What this document does not claim"; "What (E) does not exclude"
rows.file_10_quote: It does not supply an objective aesthetics, a probability of truth, a merit function, or a ranking of thinkers.
rows.note: Both headings verbatim, and the gloss's three items are file 10's. Elegance is Part V's "A less elegant account satisfies (E) as fully as a more elegant one with the same fidelity", and Part VII adds "That a three-line proof is shorter is not a fifth condition." Held. What this row does not carry is the theory's ground for the skill's other two exclusions, popular and said-by-an-expert: Part I's "Whether a transport is faithful on a contract is independent of whether anyone accepts it." See left_out.

rows.theory_term: normative relation (N); effect, purpose, aesthetic reason
rows.file_10_quote: a normative relation \(\mathcal N\subseteq A\times K\times\mathcal Rsn\times\mathcal V_A\) declared as a substantive input when aesthetic value is claimed. None is defined as another. The semantics does not derive \(\mathcal N\).
rows.note: Exact: "supplied from outside when claimed; not derived" is the last two sentences. Held. The other half of Part XI is used well by the skill without a row: by-domain §5 tests only "the claim that a choice *does certain jobs*", which is file 10's achievement condition, "\(\mathcal R[a,k]\neq\varnothing\land\mathcal R[a,k]\subseteq G[k]\) (AR)".

left_out.theory_notion: What an explanation is — the theory's own one-sentence definition
left_out.file_10_quote: An explanation is a **question-relevant organization of dependencies**, held to a target by a **transport** that is checked only by **what changes when things are changed**.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: the-idea-in-depth.md §1: "To explain something is to lay out **parts** that depend on each other, and to claim a **match-up** between those parts and the parts of the real thing. The match-up is checked in only one way: by **what changes when things are changed**." The clause "what changes when things are changed" is reused word for word, and this is the skill's first principle. It has no row; its pieces are scattered across rows 1, 7, 8 and 9, so a reader tracing the sentence finds four parts of it and never the sentence.

left_out.theory_notion: Obligations, and protected obligations held "fixed for the comparison"
left_out.file_10_quote: \(O_p\) is the set of obligations being addressed or protected. ... For claimed obligations \(O\) and protected obligations \(P\), fixed for the comparison,
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: The mark *fixed* ("a job or requirement the owner put outside the test, and said so") and Step 2's job tag *fixed*. Obligations are named once, inside row 5's term column, and glossed nowhere; Part XI's protected obligations, which would define *fixed* by its role in the assessment rather than by who asserted it, have no row at all. This is the one place in the theory that would have told *fixed* apart from *asserted* and from *borrowed* — the three-way confusion recorded at H57 break 2, H62's "Fixed / derived", H59's "The skill's two marks say different things about the same part", and H64 kind 1.

left_out.theory_notion: Repair, and that losses outside the protected set must be exposed
left_out.file_10_quote: (P) does not rank alternatives. Losses outside \(P\) must be exposed.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: reporting.md trap "Reporting what a change fixed and leaving out what it gave up"; testing-against-cases.md §3 "Say which layer it changed, and **what it gives up** as well as what it fixes." The first clause, "(P) does not rank alternatives", is also a second theory ground for the skill's "No scores" and "No totals, no ranking by count", alongside row 23's "counting jobs is not a warrant". No row.

left_out.theory_notion: The finite monotone theorem, and the condition it needs
left_out.file_10_quote: **Finite monotone theorem.** If \(\Gamma\) is finite, \(\mathsf S\) is upward closed, and \(\Gamma\in\mathsf S\), then the critical singletons are exactly \(\bigcup\min\mathsf S\) and the globally indispensable ones are exactly \(\bigcap\min\mathsf S\). ... No upward closure and no minimal member are assumed.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: Step 5's "**Remove** each part. Does it still do every job? Then try removing parts in pairs and groups", the marks *held* and *idle*, and the traps "Calling a part idle too soon" and "Assuming more detail is harmless". This is the theory's statement of exactly when removing one part at a time settles anything, and its own note that the condition is not assumed in general. No row states the theorem, the condition, or "critical singleton" and "globally indispensable" — which are the theory's words for *held*, the skill's commonest mark. "Deletion of \(d\) from \(\Gamma\) preserves support exactly when a minimal support omits \(d\)" is the theory's word for *idle*, also unmapped.

left_out.theory_notion: A substantive contrast must be one some admitted edit realizes
left_out.file_10_quote: An account whose only substantive contrast is one that no physically admitted edit realizes fails non-vacuity by having a silently narrowed contract.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: Step 2's requirement that each job be "put as a contrast: why this *and not that*", the question bank's "Why this and not what?", and the trap "Testing only against a fixed outcome. With nothing on the change list, any story passes." The contrastive form of a job is one of the skill's most-used moves and row 21 does not carry it; this sentence is its footing, and "contrast" is file 10's word (also Part IX: "nonconstant dependence on the represented distinction under the declared contrasts").

left_out.theory_notion: Explanatory realism — fidelity is independent of acceptance
left_out.file_10_quote: **Explanatory realism.** Whether a transport is faithful on a contract is independent of whether anyone accepts it. Systems can be wrong about their transports, their observations, their criticisms, and their own capacities.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: The stance "**Not on the list of tests:** short, simple, elegant, popular, said by an expert. None of these holds a part in place", and the question bank's dodge "The experts agree." → "What holds it in place for them? What would they swap, if they could?" Row 58 maps truth, score and elegance to Part 0 and Part V; acceptance and authority are Part I's, and have no row.

left_out.theory_notion: A question can be wrong, including by combining incompatible requirements
left_out.file_10_quote: A question may fail to pick out its alleged target, assume an incompatible baseline, or combine incompatible requirements. Its formulation is still an event.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: Step 1's "First make sure there is something to explain: \"sales dropped\" compared with what? A thing that did not happen needs no explanation" uses the first two limbs; the question bank's "Compared with what? How do we know it happened at all?" is the same. The third limb the skill never tests: *Pull* takes "the parts in pairs", and no step asks whether the *job list* fights itself. There is no row for the heading, so the untested limb is also untraced.

left_out.theory_notion: Grain, and that it is a declared index rather than a fact
left_out.file_10_quote: **Indices, not primitives.** Grain \(\ell\), boundary \(\beta\), continuity \(\Omega\), and the contract \(C\) are declared indices. Every claim is relative to them; none is a predicate that could be true or false.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: "the same explanation at this level" in SKILL.md, the stance "An explanation can be tight for one question and idle for another", and "at that grain" inside row 25's own gloss — the only place the word "grain" appears in the word list. File 10 uses grain in two senses, the physical \(\ell\) of \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) and "one account at grain \(C\)" in Derivation 2, which is the contract; the skill's "level" is the second. No row separates them, so "at this level" is traceable only by noticing which grain Derivation 2 means.

left_out.file_10_quote: A theory may contain an accurate scoped dependence together with errors elsewhere. What cannot count as explanation is an error in the very dependence alleged to do the work.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: The whole part-by-part shape of the report rather than a verdict on the whole — reporting.md's "No totals, no ranking by count. Report by job: what gets done, what fails, and because of which missing part" — and the stance "Loose is not wrong. A loose part may be true." This is why the skill marks parts instead of judging explanations, and it has no row.

left_out.theory_notion: The three provenances are told apart by history, not by output
left_out.file_10_quote: The three are distinguished by their histories, not their outputs, and the semantics keeps them apart.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: the-idea-in-depth.md §8: "The three are told apart by their history, not by their results. Two explanations can give the same outputs today and differ completely in what holds them." Near-verbatim reuse. Rows 26 to 28 map the three provenances one by one and row 46 maps the output point to Derivation 9, but the sentence that says why the skill must ask for a part's history rather than read it off the part's behaviour has no row — and it is the theory's answer to grievance 6 and its stated defeat condition (D).

left_out.theory_notion: Functional transport: fidelity on each generator gives fidelity on compositions
left_out.file_10_quote: **Functional transport.** If \(\pi\circ S_a=T_a\circ\pi\) for every generator \(a\), the same holds for every admitted finite composition with matching scopes.
left_out.where_the_skill_uses_it: "**One part and one change at a time.**" (SKILL.md, How to ask) and "One part, one change, one question. Stacked questions get stacked stories" (question-bank.md §1). This theorem is the licence for testing one change at a time, and it is what discharges the clause of (F2) that row 9 leaves out (\(\tau(a_2a_1)=\tau(a_2)\tau(a_1)\)). Neither the theorem nor the clause has a row, so the skill's rule reads as a habit of interviewing when the theory can make it a result — under a stated condition (a functional transport with matching scopes) that the skill never states.

verdict:
Two things about scope first. File 32's word list is the same file as file 31's: H67 says "Nothing else changes ... the other modules are as in file 31", and reading both found no difference (I could not run diff, being read-only, so that is a reading, not a byte check). So none of file 32's five changes touches this file, and everything below bears on 31 and 32 alike — including the fact that R2's untested half stays untested by the hardening. Second, my convention: `gloss_matches` answers whether file 10 bears out the row taken whole — plain word, term and gloss together — so a row whose gloss restates its term faithfully can still read "partly" when the plain word attached to it names a different act. Re-derive it from the quotes if you disagree with a mark; each row carries its own.

HELD, by file 10's text. The theory's account machinery comes across intact and often in the theory's own words. Organizations, admitted edits and their three forms, contracts, queries, the respect of a question (a verbatim phrase from Part XIV), transports, all four conditions of (E) with their labels, support, critical blocks, redundant routes, interference, infinitary support, boundary, Pres(F), the three provenances, violation and surprise, the two responses, identification and fibres and (I4), obstruction and (O1), eliminative explanation with its self-marked weakness passed on, the historical index and goalpost-moving, (K1) to (K3) on failure, receipts, (T2), Derivation 9, the normative relation. Five rows are held about as tightly as a plain-word gloss can be: "hard to vary; reach" carries all three clauses of file 10's sentence including "counting jobs is not a warrant", which the skill's stance and traps then repeat; "watch the part as well as the outcome" carries the measurement and causal signatures with the observation-edit clause word for word ("alters the relation reporting it without altering what it reports"); "a label does no work" carries a claim file 10 states more strongly than the row does; "what the evidence can hold in place" is (I1) in plain words with file 10's own two-scales case behind it; and "moving the goalposts" is file 10's phrase, "a failure of the record, not a licensed operation". These are not paraphrases that happen to fit. The theory's sentences are doing the work and the plain words are shorter forms of them.

LOOSE. Nine rows are held less tightly than they read, and in each the row would survive a rewording that named a nearer neighbour in file 10. "The change list is not empty" attaches to non-vacuity a failure file 10 routes through non-circular dependence. "The same explanation at this level" cites Derivation 2, whose premise is that both candidates already are accounts; the skill's actual verdict is carried by (K) and by Derivation 2's consequence. "Held if" gives a consequence of a definition in the term column, and its second sentence has no footing at all. "Parts that pull against each other" and "an added part that breaks it" both point at interference, and only the second is interference; Pull is a way of hunting it plus a boundary question that row 20 already holds. "A catch-all needs a gauge" anchors a claim about a part to a condition about the contract. "A fitted part cannot be confirmed on the cases it was fitted to" is rescued by one hedging word, "new", and reaches across from transports to measurement kernels without saying so. "Seen, claimed, recalled, worked out" builds a four-way taxonomy on a two-way distinction. "Freeze the rig" treats a test rig as a selected transport, which the theory permits and does not do. "A held limit carries its reason inside the explanation" names a construction, "hard-to-vary over scope", that is not in file 10, and points at contract edits where Part VI's family is organization edits — though the skill's test is sound, because it tests only limits inside the explanation and marks a limit that "only says what is being asked about" free. Loose here means what the skill means by it: these may all be right, and nothing yet holds them where they stand.

ASSERTED. Two rows say more than file 10 does. "The three layers of a home-made test" reads (K3) as covering a passed test; (K3) is stated for an established ¬O only, and from the implication plus O nothing follows, so the row's "failed or passed" has no licence in the cited term — while row 41, on the same term, glosses it correctly as failure alone. The skill's point is sound and belongs to Derivation 9, which the row does not cite. And "where a job came from: given, fixed, added" carries provenance from the contract down to each job, which file 10 does not do (Part VI's jobs have no provenance field); aligns three skill tags against three theory values that do not correspond, losing the theory's *selected* and *constructed* and so the skill's ability to record that a job was found rather than stipulated; and files *fixed* under "where it came from" when *fixed* answers whether a job is up for test — which file 32's own new paragraph says, in other words, when it rules that "*borrowed* and *fixed* are not provenances". Both rows' extra content may be true. Neither is in the theory.

The largest gap is not any one row. It is that the eight marks — the vocabulary every report the skill produces is written in — are the part of the skill this file maps least. *Held*, *idle*, *loose*, *borrowed* and *unknown* do not occur in file 10 (checked by search); *two routes* is the one mark with a term of its own. The theory's own words for *held* and *idle* sit in the finite monotone theorem, together with the condition (upward closure) that says when the skill's remove-one-at-a-time reasoning settles anything and the sentence "No upward closure and no minimal member are assumed" that says the condition is not free. The theory's carrier for *fixed* is a protected obligation "fixed for the comparison", named once inside a term column and glossed nowhere. *Borrowed* has no counterpart in file 10 that I could find. Every recorded fault that sits on the mark vocabulary — H57's break 2, H62's *Asserted*-as-a-mark and "Fixed / derived", H59's note that *borrowed* and *fixed* are both true of one part, H64's kinds 1 and 3 — sits on the half of the skill that is least traced. I cannot show the missing rows caused any of it: those readers had this file available and three of the reports that broke had opened it, no run gave a reader file 10, and none of the results was designed to test the mapping. What can be said is where a tightening would go, and that it would go where the trouble has been.

On the front matter's claim, "That theory's terms are mapped to plain words in `references/word-list.md`": held for the theory's testing machinery, loose in nine places named above, asserted in two, and silent on the theory's own definition of an explanation, whose words the skill reuses verbatim in its first principle with no row. The stronger half of the claim — that the skill *sharpens* Deutsch's idea *using* the theory — is not what this check tests, and R2 is right that it stays untested: I checked a mapping, not what the mapping adds. Two rows would tighten it most, and both are additions rather than corrections: one tying *held* and *idle* to the critical singletons and the deletable commitments of the finite monotone theorem, carrying its condition, so the skill's central procedure has its stated ground and its stated limit; and one tying *fixed* to a protected obligation held fixed for the comparison, so the mark is defined by its role in the assessment rather than by who said so. What this does not show: nothing here bears on whether any plain word is a good instruction, only on whether file 10 says what the row says it says; nothing bears on the theory's truth or the skill's; and a mismatch in this file is not a fault in the procedure, which several recorded readers ran well without opening it.

falsified.finding: "Global fidelity" is the skill's coinage: file 10 gives (F2) no name, presenting it under the bold heading "Component fidelity" and calling it only "the assembled organization agrees". So row 9's term column invents a name.
falsified.why_dropped: The quote is not there. Part IV, before Part V: "A transport is **faithful on \(C\)** when it satisfies the component and global fidelity conditions of Part V." The phrase is file 10's own. I had looked only where (F2) is defined and taken absence there for absence everywhere — the exact failure the skill's testing-against-cases warns of ("\"Found nowhere\" means unknown ... \"I did not find X\" describes your search"). A combined search found it at line 204.

falsified.finding: The skill's Step 1 names six kinds of question where file 10's respect list has five (production, identification, obstruction, rule-status, purpose-achievement), so the skill over-reaches the theory by adding "Why is there none of it?", and row 6 conceals it by glossing five.
falsified.why_dropped: The rival reading fits better and is the skill's own. The sixth is not offered as a respect but as the Part VII question shape, "A question of the form \"why is there no \(X\)-effect?\"", which row 36 maps explicitly ("explaining an absence" → "explanations that remove structure"). Two rows for two different places in file 10, and both hold. Nothing in row 6 is wrong and nothing in Step 1 is untraced. Kept only as a note on row 6.

falsified.finding: The skill's *Check the patches* test tells the reader to "swap the new limit for a neighbour", which varies the contract — and Part VIII and Derivation 7 say a changed contract is a new claim at a new index, not a variation whose survival can be compared inside one frozen assessment. So the skill tests what it elsewhere freezes, and row 57 hides the contradiction.
falsified.why_dropped: Swapped for the nearest rival reading of the same text and the rival won. SKILL.md distinguishes the two kinds of limit itself: "A limit that is held comes with its reason inside the explanation (the yeast slows in the cold) ... A limit that only says what is being asked about is free; say so." The limit it swaps is a commitment inside the explanation, an ordinary organization edit in Part VI's \(\mathcal V\); the contract limit it marks free and does not test. No contradiction. What survives is the much smaller point that row 57's term column says "edits to the contract" and names a construction ("hard-to-vary over scope") that is not in file 10.

falsified.finding: The skill's rule "One part and one change at a time" is unlicensed by the theory, because (F2) requires composed changes to translate to composed changes (\(\tau(a_2a_1)=\tau(a_2)\tau(a_1)\)) and the skill never pokes two things at once.
falsified.why_dropped: I asked what would show it wrong and found it in Part VIII: "**Functional transport.** If \(\pi\circ S_a=T_a\circ\pi\) for every generator \(a\), the same holds for every admitted finite composition with matching scopes." The theory proves that checking generators suffices, so the skill's rule is licensed, not unlicensed. Reversed direction: the theorem became a left_out item (the skill's rule has a result behind it and a stated condition it never states), and the omission of the clause became a note on row 9.

falsified.finding: Row 47 flatly contradicts file 32's new paragraph: the paragraph rules that "*borrowed* and *fixed* are not provenances", while the row files *fixed* under "where a job came from", which is a provenance question. File 32's change 1 therefore collides with the unchanged word list.
falsified.why_dropped: The two are not about the same object. File 32's paragraph governs marks and provenances on *parts*; row 47 tags *jobs*, and Step 2's three job tags are a third list the paragraph does not mention. So there is no flat contradiction and I dropped the collision claim. What survives, and is in row 47, is that *fixed* answers whether a job is up for test rather than where it came from, and has no counterpart among the theory's three provenances — with the theory's real carrier for it (protected obligations, "fixed for the comparison") unmapped.

falsified.finding: Row 21 mis-glosses "explanatory jobs (F)": in file 10 each \(f\) occupies the slot of a question \(p\) in Account(·,·), so a job is a question with its own contract and query, not "the things the explanation has to account for".
falsified.why_dropped: Removing the finding changes nothing: a question in file 10 just is a thing to be accounted for, carrying a target, a contract and a query, so the gloss is a fair plain rendering of the slot it fills. Pressing the point would demand formality from a file whose stated job is plain words. What survives is different and narrower: Step 2's contrastive requirement for a job is not in the row, and its footing in file 10 ("An account whose only substantive contrast is one that no physically admitted edit realizes fails non-vacuity") has no row. That went to left_out.

falsified.finding: The word list has no row for the eight marks, so the skill's entire reporting vocabulary is unmapped and the front matter's claim fails for it.
falsified.why_dropped: Too broad to survive its own test. Rows 15 to 20 map the machinery the marks report — support, critical block, redundant routes, interference, infinitary support, boundary — and *two routes to one job* is row 17 exactly. What survives is narrower and checkable: *held*, *idle*, *loose*, *borrowed* and *unknown* appear nowhere in file 10 (searched); the theory's own words for held and idle sit unmapped in the finite monotone theorem; and *borrowed* has no counterpart I could find. Stated that way in the verdict and in left_out item 4.

falsified.finding: Row 25 is wrong: Derivation 2 does not support the skill's "same explanation at this level" verdict, so the verdict the skill reaches (recorded in six reports in file 54 and in seven of twelve in H57) has no theory behind it.
falsified.why_dropped: The consequence clause of the same Derivation supports it: "A claim that two such candidates \"really\" differ is a claim that some admitted change separates them, and must supply it", and (K)'s definition of one kind on \(C\) carries the rest without needing accounthood. So the verdict stands and the theory backs it. What survives is only that the row cites the premise-heavier half of Derivation 2 rather than the half the skill uses — a mis-citation, not a false claim, and marked "partly" rather than "no".

falsified.finding: The skill's "count the patches" (testing-against-cases) contradicts the theory's ban on counting, "counting jobs is not a warrant", and its own stance "No scores. Do not count confirmations, jobs or parts."
falsified.why_dropped: Different objects. File 10's ban is on counting *jobs* as a warrant of hardness; counting patches is a diagnostic of how much a rig was tuned, which bears on the rig's provenance, and the skill never adds it into a verdict. Removing the finding changes nothing about either text. What survives is only that the phrase has no term in file 10, noted on row 54.

falsified.finding: Row 50's gauge requirement is an invention with no theory behind it and should be marked as unsupported.
falsified.why_dropped: The row says so itself — "and here also measured" marks the addition — and the skill's own test for an addition is met: "does it help find what holds a part in place, or what would?" A gauge is exactly a thing that would. Judging it unsupported would be demanding tightness from something honestly declared as the skill's own. What survives is the smaller point that the anchor looks wrong: a catch-all is a part that constrains nothing, while non-vacuity is a condition on the contract, so Part II's full relation on a deleted component's ports, or non-circularity's demand for a change that moves the answer, would hold it better.
